verdict.summary: The component-indexed lowering is coherent and complete for its documented subset. A non-ground quoted position is first captured by the ordinary pattern join, then UnpackTriple rejects non-triple IDs and binds or checks components left-to-right. Compiler bound-state handling correctly makes repeated variables, variables shared with a plain position in the same atom, and variables correlated from earlier atoms checks rather than destructive rebindings. Nested object quotations are emitted after their parent unpack, and semi-naive delta indices continue to identify Pattern steps rather than deferred unpack steps. Ground quoted terms use the same Dict structural interning path as loaded data, while unsupported variable-bearing conclusions, negation bodies, and structurally impossible triple terms fail loudly. The tests exercise real compile/bind/eval paths and cover constants, correlation, repeated variables, opacity, nesting, derived-fact rounds, and rejection cases; they are not vacuous. Documentation matches the implemented envelope. No security or correctness defect was found. The targeted test could not be run in this environment because cargo is unavailable.
